edits.before: Irelia has no way to close the gap on you safely at levels 1-2 — her only engage is Bladesurge off a minion, and Twin Drift plus The Weirding's slow means she eats a full combo for every attempt. Keep your wave manipulated so she can't get a free Q reset off low-health casters, and chip her with Q pokes she can't answer. She's forced into passive farming almost every wave.
edits.after: Level 1 is hers and there is no clever way around it: Bladesurge dashes 600 off any minion, heals her on the way in, and refreshes if the target dies to it. Keep the low caster off your side of the wave so the reset has nowhere to land, poke with Q at 900, and take the farm. From 3 the loop exists — E for the slow and the backhop out — and the trade ends before Flawless Duet can hold you.

notes: The level chart already agrees across both layers on all seven rows (Irelia throughout), so no side/win edits were needed and none are proposed. FLAG FOR THE USER: packet.levelChart for this matchup reads all-Aurora, disagreeing with the page on every row and with a 49.7% win rate on an 8/10 HARD matchup. I left the rows alone per the chart rule; someone should decide which extract is authoritative. The worst defect here was the `early` paragraph flatly contradicting its own chart — it told the reader Irelia has no safe way to close at levels 1-2 while every other field on the page gives her those levels, and the kit agrees with the fields (Bladesurge is a 15-mana 600-range dash onto any unit that heals her). Two Aurora ability names on this page, "Twin Drift" and "The Weirding", could not be verified against the ownerKit, which lists Aurora's slots without names; rather than guess a replacement I rewrote both sentences into the slot-based voice used everywhere else on the page. Pronouns correct throughout (Irelia is female). lintFindings was empty.
